clue.text: Panic as displayed by marines?

parts.note: à la means in the style or manner of, as something is shown by
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the marines are showing fear.
explanation.walkthrough: À LA (French, 'in the manner of') plus RM, the Royal Marines, Britain's commando force.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden fright or panic is a synonym, as in 'the news caused alarm'.

clue.text: Something often considered fixed when fixed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
set means fixed or firmly established

explanation.surface: A riddling remark about something regarded as permanent once it has been settled.
explanation.walkthrough: Accountants speak of fixed assets, such as buildings and machinery, which is why the definition carries the word 'fixed'.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounting, property or equipment held long-term is classed as a fixed resource of value.

clue.text: Disposition to include one after morning in the environment

indicators.note: the bent-with-one piece follows the morning abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

indicators.note: the word for disposition takes in the letter for one

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination or disposition
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A temperament that settles in after the morning, in some setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes surrounding conditions, such as the temperature or noise of a place.

clue.text: What you want to hear c/o some tunes and airs, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged in another way

parts.note: c/o, short for care of, supplies C and O along with the words some tunes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something addressed care of some tunes and airs might well be pleasant listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of C/O SOME TUNES plus AIRS; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes welcome news, exactly the kind of thing a person longs to be told.

clue.text: Regret capturing a lot of argument with supporter swearing

indicators.note: the word for regret holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: pity, as in 'what a pity', expresses regret

indicators.note: the supporter follows the trimmed argument
only most of the word for argument is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a row is a noisy argument
a fan is a supporter

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a heated row with a fan that descended into cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the final letter of the argument word, and 'capturing' puts that plus the supporter inside the regret word.
explanation.definitionFit: Profanity is foul or blasphemous language, the same thing as cursing.

clue.text: Setter to secure wine after store ultimately fooled around

indicators.note: the wine comes after the last letter of store

parts.note: Phi is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter
to land is to secure, as in landing a contract

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of store

parts.note: red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: The setter goes to buy wine after the shop and ends up messing around.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to have casual affairs, a sense of messing about romantically.

clue.text: Have current name used later

indicators.note: the letter for name is shifted to a later position in the word for current

parts.note: now means current, at present

explanation.surface: An instruction to use the current name later on.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, a straightforward synonym of having.

clue.text: Dreadful tat affects aroma, really

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are in a terrible state and need reordering

explanation.surface: Cheap tat genuinely spoils the smell of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to mean in fact or actually, matching really in emphasis.

clue.text: Progressing on board?

definitions.meaning: aboard a railway carriage, taken literally

explanation.surface: Someone is making headway while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means under way, and literally describes a passenger aboard a railway carriage.

clue.text: Certainly still upset about dietary allowance recently

parts.note: yes means certainly

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the allowance
in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not done yet'
RDA stands for recommended daily allowance

explanation.surface: Someone confirms their diet plan was recently disrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the word for still upside down, giving TEY, and 'about' wraps that round the allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: Used loosely as an adverb, the word means in the recent past, not long ago.

clue.text: Saint, upset by book in main, becoming martyr pointedly

indicators.note: by means next to, so the scrambled word comes beside
the book letter sits inside the word for main

parts.note: the main is the open sea

indicators.note: upset signals the letters of saint are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A saint, overturned by a book at sea, ends up a martyr.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint' is not ST here: 'upset' scrambles its five letters into STIAN, placed 'by' (beside) the book-in-main piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The early Christian martyr was famously shot with arrows, hence 'pointedly'.

clue.text: A soprano carrying line to other singers

indicators.note: A and S hold the next letters between them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soprano takes a musical line across to the rest of the choir.
explanation.definitionFit: In a choir, the lower female or high male voices form a separate part from sopranos.

clue.text: Emphatic charm following curtailed attempt

indicators.note: the word for charm comes after the shortened attempt
curtailed means docked of its tail, losing the last letter

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to enchant is to charm

explanation.surface: Charm used forcefully after a half-hearted try.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means incisive and forceful, as in a vigorous, emphatic criticism.

clue.text: I've been looking everywhere, just like I said

definitions.meaning: said on finally finding someone being searched for
said when proved right, meaning 'I told you so'

explanation.surface: Someone, exasperated after a search, insists they were right all along.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation greets a person found at last and also claims vindication for a prediction.

clue.text: Core of plant yielded source of tequila

indicators.note: the core is the central letter of plant

parts.note: gave means yielded, as in gave way

explanation.surface: The heart of a plant produced the raw material for tequila.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is distilled from the blue variety of this succulent desert plant.

clue.text: Work round it, going to a back courtyard

indicators.note: back means the whole construction is read in reverse
the word for work goes around the other letters

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for landscaping: work around it, taking a path to a back yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts the work abbreviation around IT and A, making OITAP, which 'back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area beside a house, like a small courtyard.

clue.text: Having wine following stew in case

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
an olio is a spicy stew

explanation.surface: Wine served after a stew, in a particular instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat carrying case for documents or drawings.

clue.text: Went back to Edward with the bass voice

indicators.note: back tells you to read the word for went in reverse

parts.note: to go can mean to urinate, so went is peed
taken as written
Ned is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone returned to Edward, the one with the low singing voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' looks like plain travel but is the slang sense, PEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-toned describes a low, resonant sound such as a bass singer produces.

clue.text: Plant, one revived with river water

indicators.note: revived suggests the letters are brought back in fresh form

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, followed by water as written

explanation.surface: A plant brought back to life by a dose of river water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revived' reworks the letters of ONE, R for river, and WATER together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash is a small tree bearing red berries, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Lecturer significantly restricted by negligible prosperity

indicators.note: the inner pieces are hemmed in by the word for negligible

parts.note: wee means tiny, so negligible
far means by a large amount, as in far better

explanation.surface: An academic is badly held back by a tiny budget, affecting their well-being.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare means well-being, health and good fortune, close to prosperity.

clue.text: Odd bits of rain and clouds offering some danger

indicators.note: the first and third letters of rain are taken

parts.note: the sky is where clouds are, so clouds stands for it

explanation.surface: Patches of rain and cloud suggest the weather may turn hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risky carries a chance of harm, the same as being somewhat dangerous.

clue.text: Banksy's penultimate source of graffiti provides surprise

indicators.note: penultimate means last but one, taken from the artist's name

parts.note: a tagger is someone who sprays graffiti tags

explanation.surface: The street artist Banksy's latest-but-one graffiti piece causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: The second-last letter of BANKSY is S; the possessive 's is just surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or amaze them greatly.

clue.text: Group of cats engaged in strife — listen

indicators.note: the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Cats fighting noisily, with someone urging others to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Felis is the zoological genus of small cats, including the domestic cat.

clue.text: Support for opening party far more doubtful

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: doubtful suggests the letters are uncertain and should be rearranged

explanation.surface: Backing for a party's launch looks much more uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: The frame around a doorway holds up the door, a support for an entrance.

clue.text: Planet core hard to shift

indicators.note: the letter for hard is moved to another place in the word for core

parts.note: the heart is the core of something
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A planet whose molten core is hard to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shift' takes the H of HEART to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Our home world is the third planet from the Sun.

clue.text: Asian city has to be adopted by US city

indicators.note: the word has is taken into the city abbreviation

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: An Asian city is twinned with an American one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, a city in Asia.

clue.text: Staff mostly rage in oil industry city

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for staff

parts.note: a stave is a staff or stick
anger means rage

explanation.surface: Most employees are furious in the petroleum business.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavanger, in Norway, is the hub of the North Sea petroleum business.

clue.text: It may be almost set?

parts.note: a riddle about the bright body in the sky, which sinks towards the horizon each evening

explanation.surface: A riddle about something nearly ready or nearly fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like readiness, but it is the daily sinking below the horizon at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: The star at the centre of our solar system is often seen low and setting in the evening.

clue.text: Reverence is adopted by head in old church

indicators.note: the head piece sits between the letters for old and church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the word is taken into the slang word for head

parts.note: bean is slang for head

explanation.surface: Respect is shown by the head of an old church.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a gesture of deep respect, such as a bow, hence reverence.

clue.text: It will light up church behind hill

indicators.note: the church abbreviation comes behind the hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A church beyond the hill will be lit up.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable lamp, something carried to illuminate a dark place.
